subject: Logic
title: Black Swan Events
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Black Swan Events.

hook.text: Before 2008, most financial models said a global banking collapse was virtually impossible. Then it happened.

buildup.text: Nassim Taleb coined Black Swan for rare, extreme events that standard models can't predict.

discovery.text: Black Swans have three properties: rarity, extreme impact, and retrospective predictability—we explain them after.

twist.text: Our models assume normal distributions. But real life has fat tails—extreme events happen far more than models expect.

climax.text: You can't predict Black Swans, but you can build systems that survive or even benefit from them.

quiz.question: What defines a Black Swan event?
options: A rare event with extreme impact that seems predictable only in hindsight
